Plotly Express arguments

Source: R/express-doc.R
px_args.Rd

Arguments shared by the Plotly Express functions; see px_scatter() and the other functions in the family.

Arguments

data_frame

A data.frame, data.table, list or matrix. Needed for column names to be used in the other arguments; if NULL, a data frame is built from the vectors given in the other arguments.

x

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the x axis in cartesian coordinates.

y

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the y axis in cartesian coordinates.

color

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign color to marks.

symbol

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign symbols to marks.

size

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign mark sizes.

hover_name

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector appear in bold in the hover tooltip.

hover_data

Extra data to show in the hover tooltip: column names (a character vector or a formula such as ~c(a, b)), or a named list with column names as names and values TRUE (default formatting), FALSE (hide the column, e.g. one shown by default), a d3-format string such as ":.3f", a vector of data, or a list of a format string or TRUE and a vector of data.

custom_data

Column names (a character vector or a formula such as ~c(a, b)), or a list of column names, formulas and vectors. Values from these columns are added to the traces' customdata (e.g. for use in Shiny events) without appearing in the hover tooltip.

text

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector appear in the figure as text labels.

facet_row

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign marks to facetted subplots in the vertical direction.

facet_col

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign marks to facetted subplots in the horizontal direction.

facet_col_wrap

Maximum number of facet columns. Wraps the column variable at this width, so that the column facets span multiple rows. Ignored if 0, and forced to 0 if facet_row or a marginal is set.

facet_row_spacing

Spacing between facet rows, in paper units. Default is 0.03 or 0.07 when facet_col_wrap is used.

facet_col_spacing

Spacing between facet columns, in paper units Default is 0.02.

error_x

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to size x-axis error bars. If error_x_minus is NULL, error bars will be symmetrical, otherwise error_x is used for the positive direction only.

error_x_minus

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to size x-axis error bars in the negative direction. Ignored if error_x is NULL.

error_y

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to size y-axis error bars. If error_y_minus is NULL, error bars will be symmetrical, otherwise error_y is used for the positive direction only.

error_y_minus

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to size y-axis error bars in the negative direction. Ignored if error_y is NULL.

animation_frame

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign marks to animation frames.

animation_group

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to provide object-constancy across animation frames: rows with matching animation_groups will be treated as if they describe the same object in each frame.

category_orders

Named list mapping column names to the order of their values in axes, legends and facets, e.g. list(day = c("Thur", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")). By default values appear in the order first encountered, or in level order for factors.

labels

Named character vector or list mapping column names to the labels to use for axis titles, legend entries and hover text, e.g. c(gdpPercap = "GDP per capita").

orientation

(default "v" if x and y are provided and both continuous or both categorical, otherwise "v"("h") if x(y) is categorical and y(x) is continuous, otherwise "v"("h") if only x(y) is provided)

color_discrete_sequence

Character vector of colors, e.g. px_colors$qualitative$Set1. Values of color are assigned colors in order (cycling), unless set in color_discrete_map. Defaults to the template's colorway.

color_discrete_map

Named character vector or list mapping values of color to colors, overriding color_discrete_sequence. If the values of color are colors, px_identity() (or "identity") uses them directly.

color_continuous_scale

Character vector of colors, e.g. px_colors$sequential$Viridis, or the name of a scale in px_colors. Used when color is numeric. Defaults to the template's sequential colorscale.

range_color

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the continuous color scale.

color_continuous_midpoint

If set, computes the bounds of the continuous color scale to have the desired midpoint. Setting this value is recommended when using plotly.express.colors.diverging color scales as the inputs to color_continuous_scale.

symbol_sequence

Strings should define valid plotly.js symbols. When symbol is set, values in that column are assigned symbols by cycling through symbol_sequence in the order described in category_orders, unless the value of symbol is a key in symbol_map.

symbol_map

Named character vector or list mapping values of symbol to marker symbols, overriding symbol_sequence. px_identity() uses the values of symbol directly.

opacity

Value between 0 and 1. Sets the opacity for markers.

size_max

Set the maximum mark size when using size.

marginal_x

One of "rug", "box", "violin", or "histogram". If set, a horizontal subplot is drawn above the main plot, visualizing the x-distribution.

marginal_y

One of "rug", "box", "violin", or "histogram". If set, a vertical subplot is drawn to the right of the main plot, visualizing the y-distribution.

trendline

One of "ols" (ordinary least squares regression), "lowess" (locally weighted smoothing), "rolling", "expanding" or "ewm" (exponentially weighted moving average). A trendline is drawn for each discrete color/symbol group; configure it with trendline_options. Fitted OLS models are available from px_get_trendline_results().

trendline_options

Named list of options for the trendline function: for "ols", add_constant, log_x and log_y; for "lowess", frac; for "rolling", window, min_periods, center and function ("mean", "median", "sum", "min", "max", "std", "var", "count"); for "expanding", min_periods and function; for "ewm", one of com, span, halflife or alpha, and adjust.

trendline_color_override

Valid CSS color. If provided, and if trendline is set, all trendlines will be drawn in this color rather than in the same color as the traces from which they draw their inputs.

trendline_scope

If "trace", then one trendline is drawn per trace (i.e. per color, symbol, facet, animation frame etc) and if "overall" then one trendline is computed for the entire dataset, and replicated across all facets.

log_x

If TRUE, the x-axis is log-scaled in cartesian coordinates.

log_y

If TRUE, the y-axis is log-scaled in cartesian coordinates.

range_x

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the x-axis in cartesian coordinates.

range_y

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the y-axis in cartesian coordinates.

render_mode

One of "auto", "svg" or "webgl", default "auto" Controls the browser API used to draw marks. "svg" is appropriate for figures of less than 1000 data points, and will allow for fully-vectorized output. "webgl" is likely necessary for acceptable performance above 1000 points but rasterizes part of the output. "auto" uses heuristics to choose the mode.

title

The figure title.

subtitle

The figure subtitle.

template

A template name (see template_names()) or a template list. Defaults to default_template().

width

The figure width in pixels.

height

The figure height in pixels.

z

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the z axis in cartesian coordinates.

histfunc

One of "count", "sum", "avg", "min", or "max". Function used to aggregate values for summarization (note: can be normalized with histnorm).

histnorm

One of "percent", "probability", "density", or "probability density" If NULL, the output of histfunc is used as is. If "probability", the output of histfunc for a given bin is divided by the sum of the output of histfunc for all bins. If "percent", the output of histfunc for a given bin is divided by the sum of the output of histfunc for all bins and multiplied by 100. If "density", the output of histfunc for a given bin is divided by the size of the bin. If "probability density", the output of histfunc for a given bin is normalized such that it corresponds to the probability that a random event whose distribution is described by the output of histfunc will fall into that bin.

nbinsx

Positive integer. Sets the number of bins along the x axis.

nbinsy

Positive integer. Sets the number of bins along the y axis.

text_auto

If TRUE or a string, the x or y or z values will be displayed as text, depending on the orientation A string like ".2f" will be interpreted as a texttemplate numeric formatting directive.

line_group

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to group rows of data_frame into lines.

line_dash

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign dash-patterns to lines.

line_dash_sequence

Strings should define valid plotly.js dash-patterns. When line_dash is set, values in that column are assigned dash-patterns by cycling through line_dash_sequence in the order described in category_orders, unless the value of line_dash is a key in line_dash_map.

line_dash_map

Named character vector or list mapping values of line_dash to dash patterns, overriding line_dash_sequence. px_identity() uses the values of line_dash directly.

markers

If TRUE, markers are shown on lines.

line_shape

One of "linear", "spline", "hv", "vh", "hvh", or "vhv"

pattern_shape

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to assign pattern shapes to marks.

pattern_shape_sequence

Strings should define valid plotly.js patterns-shapes. When pattern_shape is set, values in that column are assigned patterns-shapes by cycling through pattern_shape_sequence in the order described in category_orders, unless the value of pattern_shape is a key in pattern_shape_map.

pattern_shape_map

Named character vector or list mapping values of pattern_shape to pattern shapes, overriding pattern_shape_sequence. px_identity() uses the values directly.

groupnorm

One of "fraction" or "percent". If "fraction", the value of each point is divided by the sum of all values at that location coordinate. "percent" is the same but multiplied by 100 to show percentages. NULL will stack up all values at each location coordinate.

base

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position the base of the bar.

barmode

One of "group", "overlay" or "relative" In "relative" mode, bars are stacked above zero for positive values and below zero for negative values. In "overlay" mode, bars are drawn on top of one another. In "group" mode, bars are placed beside each other.

x_start

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). (required) Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the x axis in cartesian coordinates.

x_end

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). (required) Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the x axis in cartesian coordinates.

marginal

One of "rug", "box", "violin", or "histogram". If set, a subplot is drawn alongside the main plot, visualizing the distribution.

barnorm

One of "fraction" or "percent". If "fraction", the value of each bar is divided by the sum of all values at that location coordinate. "percent" is the same but multiplied by 100 to show percentages. NULL will stack up all values at each location coordinate.

cumulative

If TRUE, histogram values are cumulative.

nbins

Positive integer. Sets the number of bins.

lines

If FALSE, lines are not drawn (forced to TRUE if markers is FALSE).

ecdfnorm

One of "probability" or "percent" If NULL, values will be raw counts or sums. If "probability", values will be probabilities normalized from 0 to 1. If "percent", values will be percentages normalized from 0 to 100.

ecdfmode

One of "standard", "complementary" or "reversed" If "standard", the ECDF is plotted such that values represent data at or below the point. If "complementary", the CCDF is plotted such that values represent data above the point. If "reversed", a variant of the CCDF is plotted such that values represent data at or above the point.

violinmode

One of "group" or "overlay" In "overlay" mode, violins are on drawn top of one another. In "group" mode, violins are placed beside each other.

points

One of "outliers", "suspectedoutliers", "all", or FALSE. If "outliers", only the sample points lying outside the whiskers are shown. If "suspectedoutliers", all outlier points are shown and those less than 4Q1-3Q3 or greater than 4Q3-3Q1 are highlighted with the marker's "outliercolor". If "outliers", only the sample points lying outside the whiskers are shown. If "all", all sample points are shown. If FALSE, no sample points are shown and the whiskers extend to the full range of the sample.

box

If TRUE, boxes are drawn inside the violins.

boxmode

One of "group" or "overlay" In "overlay" mode, boxes are on drawn top of one another. In "group" mode, boxes are placed beside each other.

notched

If TRUE, boxes are drawn with notches.

stripmode

One of "group" or "overlay" In "overlay" mode, strips are on drawn top of one another. In "group" mode, strips are placed beside each other.

error_z

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to size z-axis error bars. If error_z_minus is NULL, error bars will be symmetrical, otherwise error_z is used for the positive direction only.

error_z_minus

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to size z-axis error bars in the negative direction. Ignored if error_z is NULL.

log_z

If TRUE, the z-axis is log-scaled in cartesian coordinates.

range_z

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the z-axis in cartesian coordinates.

a

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the a axis in ternary coordinates.

b

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the b axis in ternary coordinates.

c

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the c axis in ternary coordinates.

r

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the radial axis in polar coordinates.

theta

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks along the angular axis in polar coordinates.

direction

One of "counterclockwise" or "clockwise". Default is "clockwise" Sets the direction in which increasing values of the angular axis are drawn.

start_angle

Sets start angle for the angular axis, with 0 being due east and 90 being due north.

range_r

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the radial axis in polar coordinates.

range_theta

If provided, overrides auto-scaling on the angular axis in polar coordinates.

log_r

If TRUE, the radial axis is log-scaled in polar coordinates.

line_close

If TRUE, an extra line segment is drawn between the first and last point.

lat

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks according to latitude on a map.

lon

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to position marks according to longitude on a map.

locations

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are to be interpreted according to locationmode and mapped to longitude/latitude.

locationmode

One of "ISO-3", "USA-states", or 'country names' Determines the set of locations used to match entries in locations to regions on the map.

geojson

GeoJSON as a list (e.g. from jsonlite::read_json()), with features whose ids are referenced by locations.

featureidkey

Path to field in GeoJSON feature object with which to match the values passed in to locations.The most common alternative to the default is of the form 'properties.<key>.

projection

One of "equirectangular", "mercator", "orthographic", "natural earth", "kavrayskiy7", "miller", "robinson", "eckert4", "azimuthal equal area", "azimuthal equidistant", "conic equal area", "conic conformal", "conic equidistant", "gnomonic", "stereographic", "mollweide", "hammer", "transverse mercator", "albers usa", "winkel tripel", "aitoff", or "sinusoidal"Default depends on scope.

scope

One of "world", "usa", "europe", "asia", "africa", "north america", or "south america"Default is "world" unless projection is set to "albers usa", which forces "usa".

center

Dict keys are "lat" and "lon" Sets the center point of the map.

fitbounds

One of FALSE, locations or geojson.

basemap_visible

Force the basemap visibility.

zoom

Between 0 and 20. Sets initial map zoom level. Higher values are more zoomed-in. If not provided, the map will select its own zoom level.

map_style

Identifier of base map style. Allowed values are "basic", "carto-darkmatter", "carto-darkmatter-nolabels", "carto-positron", "carto-positron-nolabels", "carto-voyager", "carto-voyager-nolabels", "dark", "light", "open-street-map", "outdoors", "satellite", "satellite-streets", "streets", "white-bg".

radius

Sets the radius of influence of each point.

dimensions

Column names in data_frame (a character vector or a formula such as ~c(a, b)), or a list of column names, formulas and vectors. Values from these columns are used for multidimensional visualization.

dimensions_max_cardinality

When dimensions is NULL and data_frame is provided, columns with more than this number of unique values are excluded from the output. Not used when dimensions is passed.

names

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used as labels for sectors.

values

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to set values associated to sectors.

hole

Number between 0 and 1: the fraction of the radius cut out of the pie to make a donut chart.

parents

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used as parents in sunburst and treemap charts.

path

Column names in data_frame (a character vector or a formula such as ~c(a, b)), or a list of column names, formulas and vectors. The columns define the hierarchy of sectors, from root to leaves. Cannot be combined with ids or parents.

ids

A column name in data_frame, a vector of values, a one-sided formula evaluated in data_frame (e.g. ~ log(pop)), px_constant() or px_range(). Values from this column or vector are used to set ids of sectors

branchvalues

"total" or "remainder" Determines how the items in values are summed. Whenset to "total", items in values are taken to be valueof all its descendants. When set to "remainder", itemsin values corresponding to the root and the branches:sectors are taken to be the extra part not part of thesum of the values at their leaves.

maxdepth

Positive integer Sets the number of rendered sectors from any given level. Set maxdepth to -1 to render all thelevels in the hierarchy.
